text:
anya: FYI — nightly evals (sdq-stability) flagged a big regression after the v22.4 weight + tokenizer merge. lots of broken prefix behavior and shifted tokens in generated JSONs.

anya: quick example from nightly run 30789: input prompt (truncated): "Summarize:", expected keys: [title, summary], got: {"sumary": ...} with token offsets off by 1.

anya: hypothesis: tokenizer merge changed some merge-rules -> token ids shifted for certain prefixes. KV-prefix caching then replays wrong offsets and corrupts continuation.

sam: can you paste the exact failing sample and the tokenizer config used for that run?

anya: pasted one below. small reproduction from sample 30789-41.

anya: ```
PROMPT: "Summarize: The quarterly report shows..."
MODEL: v22.4-int4-quantized (tokenizer: merged-bpe-2026)
OBSERVED: "{\"sumary\": \"Q3 grew by 12%...\"}"
EXPECTED: "{\"summary\": \"Q3 grew by 12%...\"}"
NOTES: token boundaries around "summary" appear to have recombined (sum + ary -> sumary id changed)
```

jen: i looked at the tokenizer commit — it removed an explicit merge pair for "mar"->"mar@@" and tightened normalization. that could shift shortword merges. commit 8f7a3b.

mike: do we see this on hosted canary or only nightly evals?

anya: only showed up in nightly evals so far (batch of 10k prompts). quick manual canary run on a few keys didn't reproduce 100% but showed ~40% flaky examples.

eval-bot: metric snapshot: structured-output pass rate
- v22.3: 98.1%
- v22.4-int4: 63.7%
regression start time: 3078880000, failing promptset tags: sdq-stability, json-struct-ops

sam: possible mitigation paths: revert tokenizer merge (fast), build compatibility mapping table (more work), or disable KV-prefix caching so offsets don't persist (cheap immediate mitigate). which should we try first?

jen: i'll roll revert tokenizer in canary for tokenizer merge today (will create a canary build pinned to v22.4 weights + v22.3 tokenizer). that will let us isolate weights vs tokenizer.

mike: also try disabling KV-prefix caching on a small canary traffic slice. if symptoms vanish we know caching + token id change interaction is root cause.

anya: i'll prepare the minimal reproducer and upload promptset to s3://redwood-evals/repro/3078901234.zip (contains 200 failing prompts).

sam: thanks — can you include the exact tokenization output (ids + tokens) for a few failing items? that'll help diff.

anya: yep will include a small table in the zip. example tokenization (v22.3 vs merged):
```
input: "summary"
v22.3 -> [ 45, 1023 ] tokens: ["sum", "mary"]
v22.4 -> [ 47 ] tokens: ["sumary"]
```

jen: that aligns with my read of the commit. merging behavior produced fewer tokens for that word, shifting subsequent token ids.

mike: note: quantized kernel uses token-offset assumptions in kv cache indexing. if number of tokens differs across encoder vs kv mapping we can get off-by-one when resuming generation.

sam: ok action items: jen revert tokenizer in canary (ETA 3h), mike create a KV-disabled canary flag and run 2k prompts (ETA 6h), anya upload reproducer (ETA 1h). sam to own triage doc and roll-back decision.

deploy-bot: canary deploy triggered: revert-tokenizer-canary -> job 5621 (jen).

anya: thanks. after revert i'll re-run the nightly eval locally to confirm. if pass rate recovers we schedule a coordinated rollout to main.

sam: if revert fixes it we should add a compatibility shim to tokenization layer before merging again — mapping some common token pairs to stable ids. long-term we need automated tokenizer-compat checks in the onboarding pipeline.

mike: agreed. add a unit that compares tokenization on anchor promptsets and fails onboarding if tokenization delta > threshold.

anya: uploaded repro (s3 link included) and token id dumps. starting local rerun now.

jen: canary revert is up (job 5621 completed). monitoring metrics.

eval-bot: canary snapshot after revert (1h): structured-output pass rate on repro set = 96.8% (baseline 98.1).

sam: good signal. i'll draft rollback + compatibility plan in the triage doc and loop legal/compliance if we need an emergency patch.

mike: also add a short note to the release checklist: "double-run tokenization diff vs previous stable when changing merges/normalization".

anya: great. thanks everyone. will follow up with final numbers in the triage doc. :thumbsup:
